ch06:label: Chapter 6
ch06:title: The Sons of God
ch06:0: The administration of the universe examined in Chapter 5 rests on a single fact: the Universal Father entrusts to his Sons everything that another can do. Who, then, are these Sons? In The Urantia Book, ‘Son of God’ is not the title of a single being but the name of many orders that fill the universe. There are Sons who build universes and Sons who judge the ages, Sons who teach, Sons who rule, and Sons who carry life. And at the very end of the line stands man, who becomes a son by faith.
ch06:1: This chapter asks three questions. What is sonship, and into what orders is it divided? For what purpose do the Sons come down? And in what sense is man called a son of God? The answers come together in a single picture: the Sons who descend from above meeting the sons who ascend from below.
ch06:3: Paper 20 divides the Sons of God into three categories according to their origin and their path: descending Sons, ascending sons, and Trinitized Sons. The basis of this division is not higher or lower rank but the way in which their sonship was obtained.

ch06:5.cap: Table 6.1  The Three Categories of the Sons of God
rows: Creator Sons, Magisterial Sons, Trinity Teacher Sons, Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, Lanonandeks, Life Carriers
Achieved by experiential participation in evolution
Father-, Son-, and Spirit-fused mortals, evolutionary seraphim, ascending Material Sons, translated midwayers, personalized Adjusters
Embraced by the Trinity and devoted to Trinity service
Mighty Messengers, Those High in Authority, Those without Name and Number, and others

ch06:6: These three categories are not cut off from one another. The descending Sons come down to help the ascending sons, and some of the ascending sons, after reaching Paradise, are embraced by the Trinity and serve the universe once more. The three categories of sonship form one great circuit.
ch06:7: 2. The Paradise Sons: Building, Judging, and Teaching
ch06:8: At the top of the descending Sons are three orders that come directly from the Paradise Deities. Their mission, in a word, is to help those below. The descending Sons are there “to facilitate the progress in the Paradise climb of the lowly creatures of evolutionary origin—the ascending sons of God” (20:1.1). These three orders differ in origin, but in their work they are one.
ch06:10: The first order, the Creator Sons, the Michaels, are the builders of the local universes.
ch06:12: Yet the power of a Creator Son is not unlimited. In his own universe he is, for all practical purposes, God, but certain domains of creation remain in the hands of the Paradise sources. Above all, no Son can create personality. Paper 21 sets out these limits in three directions.

ch06:13.cap: Table 6.2  The Creative Powers of a Creator Son and Their Limits
rows: What the Creator Son must do
Obtain the consent and co-operation of the Infinite Spirit before creating any new type of thing
Obtain the consent of the Eternal Son before creating any new type of being
The Universal Father (designs and bestows it)
Personality is bestowed by the Father alone
The Ancients of Days of the superuniverse
The local universe tribunals do not decide it

ch06:14: The second order, the Magisterial Sons, the Avonals, are the Sons who close one age and open the next. They are called Magisterial Sons “because they are the high magistrates of the realms, the adjudicators of the successive dispensations of the worlds of time” (20:3.1). They awaken the sleeping survivors, bring a dispensation to its end, and at times appear on a planet in the flesh.
ch06:16: Even within the same order, every Son is unique. The universe of the Sons is not a bureaucracy of officials stamped from one mold but a family of distinct personalities serving the same will. The third order, the Trinity Teacher Sons, the Daynals, neither rule nor judge.
ch06:18: Sons who build, Sons who judge, Sons who teach: the functions of the three Paradise Sons answer, in turn, three needs—creation, justice, and enlightenment. From the time a world comes into being, through its correction age by age, until at last it awakens spiritually, these three Sons visit that world one after another. Paper 20 groups them together as “creators, servers, bestowers, judges, teachers, and truth revealers” (20:1.12). But the work of the three Sons is more than a division of labor. Each of them reveals one of the Paradise Deities to man.
ch06:20: This correspondence shows that the doctrine of the Sons follows from the doctrine of God. The Father, the Son, and the Spirit whom we examined in Part One do not remain far off on Paradise. The character of the three Deities reaches the worlds of time through the three orders of Sons. In the Creator Son man meets the character of the Father, in the Avonals the compassion of the Son, and in the Daynals the teaching of the Spirit.
ch06:21: 3. The Local Universe Sons: The Middle Links of the Descent
ch06:22: Because the Paradise Sons come from a perfect source, they do not know the conditions of the evolving worlds firsthand from the beginning. So they learn through experience, and they are helped by beings who stand closer to man than they do. Paper 20 says that when the Magisterial Sons work on the inhabited worlds, they are assisted by the Melchizedeks and the archangels. Higher Sons and lower Sons need one another. The Paradise Sons alone cannot close the whole distance between the Father and evolving man. And so the Creator Son, together with the Universe Mother Spirit, brings into being the Sons of the local universe: the Melchizedeks, the Vorondadeks, the Lanonandeks, and the Life Carriers. Among these, the Melchizedeks stand at a special place on the ladder of descent.

ch06:24.cap: Table 6.3  The Seven Orders of Descending Sons
rows: The Universal Father and the Eternal Son
Designers, creators, builders, and administrators of the local universes
The Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit
Adjudicators of the dispensations; magisterial missions and bestowal missions
The Father, the Son, and the Spirit
Educators dedicated to spiritual awakening and moral guidance
The Creator Son, the Creative Spirit, and the Father Melchizedek
The first order to serve the evolutionary races without incarnation; teachers and counselors
The Creator Son and the Creative Spirit
The Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit
The family of local universe Sons
Design creature life and carry it to the planets and plant it there

ch06:25: The Life Carriers, who occupy the lowest place among the local universe Sons, are entrusted with the most concrete task. They are responsible for the very life of a world.
ch06:27: Reading these seven orders from top to bottom reveals a principle: the farther the Sons are from the source of divinity, the closer they come to man. The Creator Son embraces a whole universe, the Planetary Prince is responsible for a single world, and the Life Carriers plant life itself on that world. The path from the Father to man is not a broken cliff but a closely spaced stairway.
ch06:29: The Lanonandeks are the Sons who rule closest to man. Being near to man, they understand the conditions of a planet well, but by the same token they are far from the Paradise source. The lower one descends, the greater the testing. Lucifer and Caligastia were Sons who fell on just this lower part of the stairway, in the Lanonandek order, and their story is told in Chapter 15.
ch06:30: 4. Bestowal: Why the Sons Come Down
ch06:31: Among the Paradise Sons, the Michaels and the Avonals come down in person to the evolutionary worlds and live as creatures of those worlds. This is called bestowal. The Urantia Book first corrects a common misunderstanding about bestowal: it is not meant to change the Father's mind.
ch06:33: Bestowal is, first of all, the Son's own experience. A ruler becomes a sympathetic ruler only by standing in the place of those he rules. And so a Creator Son must give himself seven times before he attains supreme sovereignty over his universe.
ch06:35: But bestowal is not for the Son alone. A decisive change also comes to the people of the world on which the bestowal takes place. When a bestowal Son completes his mission and returns, the Spirit of Truth is poured out, and only after that do the Thought Adjusters come to all normal human beings.

ch06:37.cap: Table 6.4  The Three Meanings of Bestowal
rows: An experiential process that makes him a sympathetic magistrate and ruler
After seven bestowals he assumes settled and supreme jurisdiction
For the people of the bestowal world
The Spirit of Truth is poured out, and Thought Adjusters indwell all normal mortals
No change (the purpose of bestowal is not to appease the Father)

ch06:38: The revelators apply the same principle to the bestowal Son's passage through the portals of death. That death is not a price paid to appease wrath but a part of completing the bestowal.
ch06:40: Michael of Nebadon completed his seventh and final bestowal on this world as Jesus of Nazareth. The meaning of that life is treated separately in Chapters 18 and 19. Here we note only that bestowal is the principle that runs through all the Sons of God. The higher the Son, the deeper he descends. The highest authority in the universe is given to the one who has personally lived in the lowest place.
ch06:41: 5. The Ascending Sons: Sonship Received by Faith
ch06:42: The descending Sons come down in order to help the ascending sons. In what sense, then, is man a son of God now? Paper 40 frankly acknowledges that man is not yet by nature of the divine order. Yet it gives man a clear status of sonship.
ch06:44: The status of faith son is not a vague consolation. Paper 40 gives five grounds on which man is called a son of God. These grounds bind together doctrines treated in other chapters of this book: faith, bestowal, the Spirit of Truth, personality, and the Adjuster.

ch06:45.cap: Table 6.5  Five Reasons Mortals Are Called Sons of God
rows: You accept the status of sonship and believe in its reality
A Creator Son of God became one of you
The spirit of a Son has been freely bestowed upon all races
Of his free will the Universal Father has given you your creature personalities
A fragment of the Universal Father dwells within you

ch06:46: Among the ascending sons there are also differences of destiny. Those who fuse with the Adjuster, those who fuse with the spirit of the Son, and those who fuse with the Spirit each follow a different path. But the revelators tell us not to read these differences as higher and lower.
ch06:48: This fact is both a privilege and a responsibility for man. If the status of sonship has been given, what remains is to live in a manner worthy of it. The Mighty Messenger who closes Paper 40 says that mortals “can now recognize your place in the family of divine sonship” (40:10.14) and can begin to sense the obligation to avail themselves of the advantages the plan provides. Even though the descending Sons have prepared everything, receiving it and walking that path remains each person's own choice. Sonship is given as a gift, but that gift becomes real only when it is received by faith.
ch06:49: In Closing: The Sons Who Descend and the Sons Who Ascend
ch06:50: The doctrine of the Sons of God is joined in a single chain. Because the Father is one who gives himself away, he works through his Sons. These Sons form a closely spaced stairway from Paradise to the planets, and they build, judge, teach, rule, and plant life. The highest Sons come down in person to live in the lowest place; through that experience they become sympathetic rulers, and their return opens to man the way of the Spirit of Truth and the Adjuster. And all this descent is for the sake of the sons who ascend from below, the human beings who have become sons by faith. One sentence of the revelators sums it all up: sonship is “the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator” (40:10.13). The next chapter examines the angels, who serve the universe alongside these Sons as the children of the Infinite Spirit.

ch06:51.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If the purpose of bestowal is not to appease the Father but to make the Son a sympathetic ruler (20:5.2), what does the experience of standing in another's place mean for those who lead others?
2. I am not yet divine by nature, yet I have the status of a faith son (40:6.1). How am I living between this ‘already’ and this ‘not yet’?
3. If God shows no partiality among ascendant destinies and loves each son alike (40:10.13), how can I let go of the habit of comparing and ranking the spiritual paths of others?

ch07:label: Chapter 7
ch07:title: Angelology
ch07:0: The Sons of God in Chapter 6 build, rule, judge, and teach the universe. But the work of the universe is not accomplished by governing alone. Alongside governing there must always be care. In The Urantia Book those entrusted with that care are the angels, the ministering spirits. If the Sons chiefly reveal the will of the Father and the Eternal Son, the angels personally carry the ministry of the Third Source and Center, the Infinite Spirit.
ch07:1: The doctrine of angels is often overlaid with imagination and legend. This chapter asks what The Urantia Book actually says about angels. Where do angels come from, and what is their nature? What do they do for man, and what do they not do? And how far does the relationship between angels and men extend?
ch07:3: The Urantia Book does not lump the angels together into a single throng. The angels are divided into seven orders spread across the three levels of the universe: the central universe, the superuniverses, and the local universes. What all of them share is service.

ch07:5.cap: Table 7.1  The Seven Orders of Ministering Spirits and Their Spheres of Service
rows: Primary: the Infinite Spirit; secondary and tertiary: the Master Spirits and the Spirits of the Circuits
The superuniverses (liaison service for the Creator Sons and the Ancients of Days)
The local universes (aids to the seraphim)
The inhabited worlds (grouped functionally with the ministering spirits)

ch07:6: The first angels man meets are the seraphim and cherubim of the local universe. They are the children of the Universe Mother Spirit. And the time of their creation is significant. The seraphim were not made as ornaments of the universe but as a provision for man.
ch07:8: When the plan for the evolution of will creatures is laid, the angels who will serve them are created along with it. From the beginning, the reason for the angels' existence is bound up with man's ascent. So angelology is at once a part of cosmology and a part of the doctrine of salvation. Moreover, the seraphim do not differ greatly in form from universe to universe. They are standard workers who can be trusted and relied upon in any universe.
ch07:10: 2. The Nature of Angels: Companions a Little Ahead of Man
ch07:11: Angels have no bodies, but that does not mean they are unreal. They are distinct individuals, and they understand human life from within.
ch07:13: The distance between angels and men is closer than we might think. Paper 38 says that in personal status angels are “not so far removed from human beings, in certain functional performances seraphim far transcend them” (38:2.3).
ch07:15: The statement that angels are ‘a trifle’ ahead of man is important. Angels are not divine beings of an entirely different dimension from man but companions walking a little ahead on the same road. When man lays aside the body and reaches the mansion worlds, he becomes very much like the angels. From this nearness comes the right attitude toward angels: they are companions to be loved, but not objects of worship.

ch07:17.cap: Table 7.2  Angels and Men: Likenesses and Differences
rows: No material body; invisible to man
Perceive man as he is in the flesh without transformers
In the first life usually unaware of angels
Created a little lower than the simpler types of angels
Far transcend man in certain functions
Companions to be loved, but not objects of worship
All are enjoined to worship God

ch07:19: The seraphim of the local universe are in turn divided into seven orders. The Infinite Spirit seeks to produce uniform seraphim, but her children appear in great variety. The differences between the orders are not differences of merit but of assignment. Paper 39 explains that even the superior seraphim receive their name not because they are qualitatively superior but “because they are in charge of the higher activities of a local universe” (39:2.1).

ch07:21.cap: Table 7.3  The Seven Orders of Local Universe Seraphim
rows: The highest of the revealed local universe angels; associated with the Seraphic Corps of Completion
In charge of the higher activities of a local universe
Devoted to the service of the constellations
The administrative duties of the local systems
Serve the Planetary Adams of the evolutionary worlds
Help in the transition from the material to the spiritual state; education on the mansion worlds
Held in reserve in preparation for the age of light and life

ch07:22: Beside the seraphim are the cherubim and sanobim who assist them. They share the seraphim's origin and resemble them in their essential endowments, but they are the lowest order of angels, and for that very reason they are man's nearest kin. Paper 38 describes them as “touchingly affectionate, and almost human” (38:7.1). In the world of angels, too, the lowly place is the near place. Following these seven orders from top to bottom, we can see that the work of the angels is arranged along a path that runs from the headquarters of the local universe through the constellations and systems to a single planet, and from that planet on to the mansion worlds. The revelators say that the farther along that path one goes, the more interesting the angels' work becomes. The ministry of angels “becomes of increasing interest as it nears the inhabited worlds, as it nears the actual problems faced by the men and women of time who are preparing themselves for the attempt to attain the goal of eternity” (39:5.1). The angelic hierarchy is a ladder of service reaching down toward man.
ch07:23: 4. The Guardians of Destiny: Angels at Man's Side
ch07:24: The relationship between angels and men is closest in the ministry of the guardian angels. Paper 113 declares that this teaching is no fancy, and it explains in concrete terms how guardian angels are assigned to human beings. The basis of assignment is not race or social standing but a person's growth in intellect and spirituality, that is, the circle he has attained. At first one angel cares for many people together.
ch07:26: As a person advances to the inner circles, the care becomes more personal. And when he reaches the third circle, a pair of seraphim is devoted to that one person alone.

ch07:28.cap: Table 7.4  The Assignment of Guardian Angels According to Circle Growth
rows: One guardian angel with one company of cherubim for one thousand people
A seraphic pair with one company of cherubim for five hundred
A pair of guardian seraphim with a group of cherubim for about one hundred
A pair of seraphim, assisted by one company of cherubim, for ten
A personal angel (in reality two) wholly devoted to one person
Conditions for being called a guardian of destiny
One or more of: a supreme decision to become Godlike, entry into the third circle, or mustering into a reserve corps of destiny

ch07:29: The task of guardianship is not forced upon the angels. They volunteer for this work, and assignments are made by weighing both the needs of the human being and the experience of the angel.
ch07:31: Nor is this relationship mere official management. The revelators say that the angels “develop an abiding affection for their human associates” (113:2.5). The guardian angel loves the person in her charge. There is a logic to this way of assignment: angelic care responds to human decision. The more a person resolves to become like God and advances to the inner circles, the more the universe answers him with personal care. The ministry of angels does not substitute for man's growth; it follows that growth and supports it.
ch07:32: 5. What Angels Do and Do Not Do
ch07:33: Angels help man, but there are clear limits to that help. Those limits exist to safeguard man's personality and free will.
ch07:35: Nor do angels act according to man's moods or requests. They follow the mandates they receive from their superiors.
ch07:37: How, then, do angels work? If the Adjuster works within, the angel works from without.
ch07:39: The situations, the people, and the opportunities a person meets, the environment that calls for decisions, are the angel's place of work. That is why angelic guidance does not promise a comfortable life. Paper 113 says that to accept the guidance of a seraphim “rarely means attaining a life of ease” (113:4.3). It is man who chooses the road; the angel helps him make the best use of it.

ch07:42.cap: Table 7.5  The Indwelling Adjuster and the Guardian Seraphim
rows: The personal agency of the ministry of the Infinite Spirit
From the outside inward, through the social, ethical, and moral environment
The essence of man's eternal nature
The teacher of man's evolving nature
Most active when the Adjuster is least active
The absent Adjuster holds the identity of the immortal being
Custodial trustee of the survival values of the sleeping soul

ch07:43: To say that angels work from without does not mean that their work is shallow. The guardian seraphim weave into one the countless influences that reach a person. On the spiritual level, they make personal many ministries of the universe that would otherwise be impersonal and prepersonal. Paper 113 describes the functions of the seraphim on three levels, spiritual, intellectual, and physical, and of these, the work on the intellectual and physical levels is as follows.
ch07:45: The working of the adjutant mind-spirits, the circuits of the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of Truth, and the work of the physical controllers do not in themselves wear the face of a personality. The angel weaves those impersonal ministries together to fit the life of a person. When the vast care of the universe reaches a single human being, it comes wearing the personal face of an angel. The Adjuster and the angel seem not to communicate with each other directly, yet they work together in perfect harmony. The presence of God guides a person from within, and the ministry of the Infinite Spirit shapes his environment from without. Between the two, man makes his own choices and grows his soul. The Adjuster is treated in detail in Chapter 11, and the soul in Chapter 12.
ch07:46: 6. A Companionship That Continues Beyond Death
ch07:47: The ministry of angels does not end at death. When a person dies, the guardian seraphim take charge of and safeguard the survival values his soul has accumulated. Resurrection on the mansion worlds is accomplished through the co-operation of the Adjuster and the seraphim. Paper 113 pictures the scene briefly: “The Adjuster will identify you; the guardian seraphim will repersonalize you and then re-present you to the faithful Monitor of your earth days” (113:6.6).
ch07:48: Upon awakening on the mansion worlds, a person sees these companions with his own eyes for the first time. And the companionship of the angels does not end there; it continues through the whole long journey of ascension. The stages of universe administration examined in Chapter 5 become the very path walked together with the angels.

ch07:50.cap: Table 7.6  The Companionship of Seraphic Guardians on the Ascension Journey
rows: Become permanent seraphic associates; witness and certify the decrees of eternal union with the Adjuster
Jerusem and the worlds of the system
Accompany the person who has attained the mature morontia estate
Edentia and its seventy spheres of socialization
Go along and pilot the person to the Melchizedeks
Bring the person to stand face to face with the Sovereign of Nebadon
The minor and major sectors and Uversa
Remain with the person to the receiving worlds, and hand him over to the seconaphim for the flight to Havona

ch07:51: And this companionship is bound up with the angels' own destiny. Angels too ascend. Angels cannot start from the very lowest place, as man does, but they can reach Paradise through the work of leading men upward.
ch07:53: Here service and ascension become one. The angel advances toward God by serving man, and man advances toward God by receiving the angel's service. The destinies of the two orders are fulfilled through each other. Of the angels who have attained Paradise, Paper 39 concludes:
ch07:55: In Closing: A Universe Joined by Service
ch07:56: The doctrine of angels can be summed up in a single chain. The angels are the children of the Infinite Spirit and the Universe Mother Spirit, created to serve will creatures when the evolution of such creatures is planned. They have no bodies, yet they are distinct personalities, companions a little ahead of man, to be loved but not worshiped. Their orders form a ladder of service from the headquarters of the local universe down to a single planet, and the care of the guardian angels becomes ever more personal in response to man's spiritual growth. They do not invade man's mind or will but work through his outward environment; beyond death they stand by him in the resurrection; and through that service they themselves attain Paradise. The universe ruled by the Sons is warmed by the service of the angels. In the next chapter we turn our gaze to examine how the material universe, the stage on which all these beings work, comes into being, from spirit through energy to matter.

ch07:57.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If angels do not invade the sanctity of the mind or manipulate the will (113:5.1), what should I hope for, and what should I not hope for, when I look for God's guidance?
2. If angels work through my social, ethical, and moral environment (113:4.1), what meaning do the situations in my life that call for decisions now carry?
3. If seraphim advance toward God by guiding a soul to the portals of Paradise (113:7.7), how is helping others connected with my own spiritual growth?

ch08:label: Chapter 8
ch08:title: The Process of Materialization
ch08:0: Chapters 5 through 7 examined the personalities who govern and serve the universe. This chapter asks about the stage on which those personalities work, the material universe itself. Where did the matter that makes up the stars, the planets, and our own bodies come from? The answer of The Urantia Book is clear: matter, too, came from God. It is not a rival principle set over against spirit but energy that has flowed out from Paradise and taken form through a series of stages.
ch08:1: This doctrine matters because it sets the relationship between matter and spirit on a right footing. If matter is seen as having nothing to do with spirit, the universe becomes a machine running on without God; if matter is seen as evil or vain, the life of the body and of the world becomes a burden to be cast off. The Urantia Book rejects both of these paths. This chapter examines in turn the source of energy, the stages by which energy becomes matter, the beings who direct that process, the structure of matter, and the principle that mind and spirit dominate matter.
ch08:3: In treating the material universe, Paper 42 first distinguishes its foundation from its essence. The universe is material in the sense that it rests on energy. But the one who upholds that material foundation is the Universal Father.
ch08:5: The foundation is material, but the essence is spirit. Paper 42 sets the two side by side in a single sentence: “The foundation of the universe is material, but the essence of life is spirit” (42:1.1). And it goes on at once to say that the Father of spirits is also the ancestor of universes. The source of spirit and the source of matter are not two but one. This energy pours forth without ceasing, and through the hands of many personalities that stream becomes matter and life.
ch08:7: Nor is the making of this energy the business of creatures. The revelators say that there is a boundary that human science, however far it advances, can never cross. Scientists will “forever will scientists be powerless to create one atom of matter or to originate one flash of energy or ever to add to matter that which we call life” (42:1.4). Man can handle and transform energy, but he can never be its source. And the energy that comes from Paradise never vanishes.
ch08:9: However endlessly its forms may change, its reality is never extinguished, and in the end it returns to the place from which it came.
ch08:11: Here the first link of the doctrine of materialization is forged. Energy comes forth from God and returns to God. Even the motion of matter is part of the great circuit of the whole universe, a purposeful stream that goes out from Paradise and returns to Paradise. Just as the structure of the universe we saw in Chapter 5 holds within it an ascent toward the center, so the energy of the universe holds within it a return to the center.
ch08:12: 2. From Space Potency to Universe Power
ch08:13: The energy that comes from Paradise does not become matter at once. Paper 42 classifies the stages through which physical energy passes into seven levels. The revelators first acknowledge that human language is too poor to distinguish these levels: “There is such paucity of language that we must assign multiple meanings to these terms” (0:6.2). And so they also give the names used on Uversa.

ch08:14.cap: Table 8.1  The Seven Levels of Force and Energy
rows: The free space presence of the Unqualified Absolute; a prereality, responsive only to the personal grasp of the Universal Father
The first basic change in space potency; sometimes called pure energy
Two phases, puissant energy (a) and gravity energy (b); the active ancestor of all universe matter
The energy of gravity control, directed into channels of power to serve the purposes of the Creators
A pre-existent stage of energy characteristic of the central universe
Operates on the upper level of Paradise and only in connection with the absonite peoples
The living, nonspirit energy of Paradise; the nonspiritual energy system of the Universal Father

ch08:15: Of the seven levels, the one man deals with directly in the universes of time and space is the fourth, universe power. Only after space-force has been changed into space-energy, and then into the energy of gravity control, is physical energy at last ready for use.
ch08:17: As the word ‘ripened’ suggests, materialization is a process of unhurried maturing. The top row of this table, space potency, the starting point of all physical energy, is a state that cannot yet even be called reality. And yet that most primal of states responds to the personal grasp of the Universal Father.
ch08:19: The very bottom of the material universe rests not on impersonal law but on the personal grasp of the Father. This is the foundation of the doctrine of materialization. The bottom row of the table is also remarkable. Monota, the nonspiritual energy of Paradise, is paired with the living spirit energy of the Eternal Son. The revelators confess that they cannot distinguish the nature of the two.
ch08:21: At their source the energies of spirit and of matter are apparently the same. They diverge only as they move away from Paradise. This is the second link of the doctrine of materialization. Matter does not spring from a root different from that of spirit; it unfolds along a different path from the same source. So the material world may be a veil that hides spiritual reality, but rightly seen it becomes a mirror that reflects that reality.
ch08:22: 3. The Living Beings Who Handle Energy
ch08:23: Energy does not become matter of itself. At every stage there are living beings who direct its transmutation. In The Urantia Book materialization is not a blind natural process but a work guided by intelligent beings.
ch08:25: The force organizers are unique beings, neither creators nor creatures, who dwell on Paradise and work in unorganized space. They are “nebulae originators” (15:4.4).
ch08:27: The spiral nebulae brought into being in this way become the mother wheels of suns and their systems. Once energy becomes responsive to gravity, the power directors take over the work. Before they are technicians who handle energy, these directors are beings whose very presence moves energy.

ch08:29.cap: Table 8.2  From Energy to Life: The Beings at Work at Each Stage
rows: Nebulae creators who manipulate the primordial space-forces; instigators of the energy cyclones
Continue the transmutation of energy from the primary to the secondary stage
Universe Power Directors (power centers and physical controllers)
Transmute energy into matter and establish the power circuits and energy channels
Materializes visible matter from pre-existent energy and establishes the inhabited realms
Initiate in dead matter the processes we call life
Perform the same work in the transition realms between the material and spiritual worlds

ch08:30: This table follows the sequence pictured in a single paragraph of Paper 42. The force organizers initiate the changes of space-force, the power directors transmute energy into matter, and thus the material worlds are born. Upon that matter the Life Carriers initiate life. The Creator Son we saw in Chapter 6 also stands in the middle of this sequence. He does not build a universe out of nothing.
ch08:32: Materialization is a co-operation of many personalities. Beings who come from the line of the Third Source and Center, the Infinite Spirit, shape the energy; the Son builds worlds from it; and the ministers of the Infinite Spirit then care for life and mind on those worlds. The material universe is a house built together by many of God's children.
ch08:33: 4. From Ultimaton to Atom: The Structure of Matter
ch08:34: When energy is organized into matter at the hands of the power directors, its first unit is the ultimaton, still unknown to the science of Urantia. Ultimatons combine to form electrons, and electrons and protons combine to form atoms. The relationship between the ultimaton and the electron is astonishingly exact.
ch08:36: Matter thus rests upon an order of number. The revelators also say that matter in all universes except the central universe is identical. The properties of matter depend on the revolutionary rates, the number, and the size of its component members, and on their distance from the nucleus. And the matter found in suns, planets, and space bodies is divided into ten classes according to its state of organization.

ch08:38.cap: Table 8.3  The Ten Grand Divisions of Matter
rows: The prime physical units of material existence; the energy particles that make up electrons
The explosive and repellent stage of the solar supergases
The electric stage of material differentiation
Existing extensively in the interior of the hot suns
Found in the cooling suns and throughout space
Individual atoms stripped of their outer electrons
The chemical stage of elemental organization; the component units of molecular or visible matter
A relatively stable state of materialization under ordinary conditions (the matter of Urantia)
Matter in which the heavier elements show a tendency to disintegrate
The relatively stationary matter found in the interior of cold or dead suns

ch08:39: In this classification, the matter man touches with his hands is only the eighth stage. The world man feels to be solid is one station on the long journey that energy travels. The revelators add that this classification follows the stages of organization rather than the appearance of things to the eyes of creatures. Matter is not a fixed thing but a state of organized energy. The process by which suns arise from nebulae and planets from suns is an extension of this same organization. The origin of the solar system to which Urantia belongs is told in detail in Paper 57.
ch08:40: 5. Spirit the Architect, Mind the Builder
ch08:41: The last link in the process of materialization is a question of direction. If energy is organized into matter, where does the pattern of that organization come from? The final section of Paper 42 finds the answer in mind and spirit. Man commonly supposes that the body comes first and that a spirit dwells within it. The revelators reverse that order.
ch08:43: The architect designs, the builder constructs, and the building stands. This figure shows at a glance the relationship of spirit, mind, and matter. Matter does not make its own patterns. The revelators call the physical “the time-space reflection of the spirit reality, the physical repercussion of the creative action of spirit-mind” (42:12.14). And they sum up this relationship in a single principle.

ch08:45.cap: Table 8.4  From Spirit to Matter: The Logical Chain of the Doctrine of Materialization
rows: Pure energy is controlled by the Universal Father, and the river of energy and life flows forth from the Deities
That which is of Paradise Deity origin has a Paradise destination
The nature of Paradise spirit and Paradise monota is apparently alike
The force organizers and power directors transmute energy and organize it into matter
Matter outside the central universe is identical and follows an exact order of number
Spirit is the architect, mind the builder, the body the building; mind dominates matter, and spirit overcontrols mind

ch08:46: This principle applies directly to man. The human body, too, is a house built by mind.
ch08:48: The body is the tabernacle in which mind dwells, and the morontia form after death is likewise individualized by that person's mind. Just as bodies differ from person to person, so do morontia forms. Through the passage from the material body to the morontia body and on to the spirit form, it is always the inner that shapes the outer. Within that body the mind grows, and when that mind follows the leading of spirit, a soul comes into being. The same section of Paper 42 adds that only the mind that freely submits itself to spirit direction can hope to survive beyond time-space existence. Mind is treated in Chapter 10, and the growth of the soul in Chapter 12.
ch08:49: In Closing: Matter Is the Shadow and the Mirror of Spirit
ch08:50: The doctrine of materialization is joined in a single chain. All energy comes from Paradise, and the Universal Father upholds it. That energy passes from space potency through primordial force and the emergent energies to become universe power, and it is organized into ultimatons, electrons, and atoms to become stars and planets. Every one of these stages is a work directed by living beings such as the force organizers, the power directors, the Creator Sons, and the Life Carriers, and its direction comes from mind and spirit. And the energy that went out from Paradise at last returns to Paradise. Matter, therefore, is not the enemy of spirit. Matter is the shadow that spirit casts upon time and space, and rightly seen, it is a mirror that reflects the reality of spirit. Man's body, and the ground on which he stands, are fragments of that mirror. With this, Part Two has examined how God governs the universe, through the order of administration, of the Sons, of the angels, and of matter. Part Three examines man himself, placed within this universe: his personality, mind, Adjuster, and soul.

ch08:51.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If it is not the body that has a spirit but the spirit that has a body (42:12.12), with what attitude should I regard my body and my material life?
2. If materialization is a work directed by intelligent beings such as the force organizers and power directors (15:4.2), how does that change the way I look at nature?
3. How is the principle that what came from Paradise returns to Paradise (42:1.8) connected with the conviction that the toil and effort of my life are not in vain?

ch09:label: Chapter 9
ch09:title: Personality
ch09:0: Part One began with God, and Part Two looked at how God governs the universe. Part Three turns to the individual human being who lives under that government. The Urantia Book does not regard man as a single undifferentiated whole. The Foreword says that human experience on Urantia contains distinct levels of reality: body, mind, spirit, soul, and personality (0:5.6–0:5.11). Four of these five each perform a work of their own, but what binds the four into one is the fifth.
ch09:2: Part Three therefore begins with personality. This chapter asks three questions. What is personality? Why does personality come only from the Universal Father? And what does the fact of personality mean for human life and destiny? Mind will be treated in Chapter 10, the Thought Adjuster in Chapter 11, and the soul in Chapter 12.

ch09:3.cap: Table 9.1  The Five Realities That Make Up Man
rows: The material organism, the living electrochemical mechanism (0:5.7)
The life mechanism prepared by material evolution (111:1.4)
The thinking, perceiving, and feeling mechanism (0:5.8)
The Third Source and Center, the bestower of mind (9:5.2)
The Thought Adjuster indwelling the mind, prepersonal in status (0:5.9)
An experiential acquirement, a morontia reality (0:5.10)
The Adjuster as father, the mind as mother (0:5.10)
The one changeless reality, the unifier of all other factors (0:5.11)
The unique bestowal of the Universal Father (0:5.11)

ch09:4: 1. Definition: Either There Is Personality or There Is None
ch09:5: The Urantia Book does not undertake to define personality. The revelator first concedes that “Personality is one of the unsolved mysteries of the universes” (5:6.2). Instead, the text makes clear what personality is not and how it is given. The most important distinction lies between mind and personality.
ch09:7: Three lines of reasoning emerge from this passage. First, personality is something added to mind. However highly mind may develop, it never becomes personality by itself. Second, personality is not a matter of degree. A person does not accumulate personality little by little but receives it whole from the start. Third, the road upward from below is closed. The Foreword says the same: “Personality is never spontaneous; it is the gift of the Paradise Father” (0:5.4). Evolution can prepare a body and a mind, but it cannot produce personality.
ch09:8: This does not mean that personality is something abstract, unrelated to the body. Personality is given from above, but the place where it functions is material life here and now. Paper 5 likens the moment personality actually begins to operate to the launching of a ship.
ch09:10: The key word here is ‘liberating.’ The Father's touch does not load anything more onto the material life vehicle; it frees that vehicle from the chain of cause and effect so that it can sail on its own. And the material self thus launched is already fully personal. A person does not become a personality only after death; while living in this body and with this mind, he already chooses, loves, and bears responsibility as a personality.
ch09:11: 2. The Ground: Why Only the Father Bestows Personality
ch09:12: Why, then, does personality come only from the Father? The ground lies in the Father's own nature. The Universal Father is neither a force nor a law. Paper 12 speaks of him in these words: “He is a freewill and primal personality” (12:7.6). Since the original of all personality exists, creature personality can only be an image derived from that original.
ch09:14: To study human personality in man alone is to look only at the shadow. The true meaning of personality must be read in the One who gives it. Paper 5 therefore calls the bestowal of personality the exclusive function of the Father and binds the relationship in both directions.
ch09:16: Personality comes from the Father and moves toward the Father. When Paper 112 describes personality as the quality “bestowed by the Universal Father himself or by the Conjoint Actor, acting for the Father” (112:0.3), the Conjoint Actor merely acts on the Father's behalf; the source of the bestowal remains the Father. The opening of Paper 5, section 6, gathers this whole relationship into one sentence: “God the Father is the bestower and the conservator of every personality” (5:6.1). The Father gives personality, preserves it, and becomes its destiny when that personality chooses his will.
ch09:17: This ground also determines the method for studying personality. To begin with human personality and infer the personality of God from it has its limits. The revelator reminds us that the direction is in fact the reverse.
ch09:19: The same section adds that better concepts of the divine personality therefore had to await the bestowal life of Michael (1:6.3). Because human and divine personality were revealed together in the life of Jesus, man obtained a clue for tracing his way back from the shadow to the substance. The relation between Jesus and personality is taken up again in Chapters 18 and 19.
ch09:20: 3. Structure: Self-Consciousness and Relative Free Will
ch09:21: How does personality show itself in a human being? Paper 16, section 8, “Urantia Personality,” names two marks.
ch09:23: Self-consciousness is more than knowing oneself. The next sentences of the same section widen its scope.
ch09:25: The ability to know oneself and the ability to know another spring from the same root. Free will is qualified by the word ‘relative.’ A person lives within the limits of body, heredity, and environment, yet the bestowal of personality “confers relative liberation from slavish response to antecedent causation” (5:6.9), and it is in precisely that opening that choice takes place. The revelator lists seven domains in which this freedom operates.

ch09:26.cap: Table 9.2  The Seven Domains of Relative Free Will
rows: Wholehearted devotion to doing the Father's will (16:8.13)
The sincere pursuit of divine values and the wholehearted love of the divine Value-Giver (16:8.14)

ch09:27: The seven domains begin with morality and end with worship. The freedom of personality is not a freedom to pick anything at all; it is a freedom to advance toward higher values. At its summit, freedom arrives at the point of giving the self to the Father.
ch09:28: The very fact of self-consciousness and free will is evidence that man cannot be explained by matter alone. Paper 112 offers this point as an answer to materialism.
ch09:30: Matter does not know itself, nor can it stand above itself and evaluate itself. That a person can look back on his life, weigh right and wrong, and choose the better shows that something given from above matter dwells within him. Paper 16 calls the full function of such a personality endowment “the beginning realization of Deity kinship” (16:8.19).
ch09:32: Another attribute of personality is uniqueness: “Personalities may be similar, but they are never the same” (16:8.4). This is not an accidental difference but a difference born of the Father's love.
ch09:34: To be unique is to be irreplaceable. Paper 112 therefore says that personalities “are associable but nontotalable” (112:0.12). Yet this uniqueness does not end in isolation. Paper 12 says that God's love for the individual is the very source of brotherhood: “This very love of God for the individual brings into being the divine family of all individuals, the universal brotherhood of the freewill children of the Paradise Father” (12:7.10). The fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man rest upon the uniqueness of personality.
ch09:35: If the Father deals with each personality in this way, how are those personalities connected with the Father? The Urantia Book answers by describing four circuits of attraction in the universe and placing the personality circuit among them.

ch09:37.cap: Table 9.3  The Four Universe Circuits and the Place of Personality
rows: All personalities, transmitting their worship to the Father

ch09:38: The personality circuit does not depend on the other three. The Father is personally conscious of, and in personal touch with, all personalities, and this personality consciousness “exists independently of the mission of the Thought Adjusters” (5:6.10). A being not indwelt by an Adjuster is still within this circuit if it has personality. Personality and the Adjuster both come from the Father, but they are different gifts. How the two work together in man is the subject of Chapters 11 and 12.

ch09:39.cap: Table 9.4  Personality and the Thought Adjuster Distinguished
rows: Proceeds directly from the Universal Father (107:1.2)
Identical in nature as it goes forth from the Father (16:8.3)
Not a personality, yet a real entity (107:7.1)
Independent of and antecedent to the Adjuster bestowal (16:8.3)
Assigned after the first moral decision (108:2.1)

ch09:41: When the Foreword says that personality “unifies all other associated factors of individuality” (0:5.11), it points to the function of personality. Paper 9 says the same: “The personality is the unifier of these components of experiential individuality” (9:4.6). If body, mind, and spirit moved separately, a human being could not be a single subject. What binds these elements into one ‘who’ is personality.
ch09:43: Thinking, feeling, and wishing can each point in a different direction. What gathers them into action in a single direction is not a part but the whole personality. Here Paper 112 distinguishes between the self and personality. The summation of the parts constitutes selfhood, that is, individuality, but such a process “has nothing whatever to do with personality, which is the unifier of all these factors as related to cosmic realities” (112:1.18). The self is what is gathered; personality is what gathers.
ch09:45: Three consequences follow from the doctrine that personality is the Father's gift. The first is fellowship. Because God and man are both persons, a communion beyond mere interaction is possible between them.
ch09:47: This fellowship is not achieved by man's dissolving into God. Because personality is unique, the way to union with God must also be a way between person and person.
ch09:49: The second is the sovereignty of choice. Once the Father has given personality, he does not force the eternal destiny of that personality. Paper 5 settles this with the word ‘decree.’
ch09:51: This sovereignty is a limit the Father has set for himself. Having given personality and provided for the growth of the soul, the Father “stands aside” (5:6.8). A coerced eternity is not what the Father desires.
ch09:53: The third is a conditioned eternity. Because personality comes from the Father, it carries the potential of eternity, but man must decide for himself whether he will take part in that eternity.
ch09:55: A person's choice, then, does not end as one person's affair. Paper 112 says that upon the fidelity of the mortal will the Adjuster depends for eternal personality, the Universal Father for the realization of a new ascending son, and the Supreme Being for the actuality of experiential evolution (112:5.5). The choice of one personality is interlocked with the whole plan of God.

ch09:56.cap: Table 9.5  The Chain of Logic in the Doctrine of Personality
rows: A quality that is neither mind nor spirit; either there is personality or there is none
Only the Father, the primal personality, bestows personality
Self-consciousness, relative free will, absolute uniqueness
Unifies body, mind, and spirit into one subject
Every personality is within the Father's personality circuit
Fellowship with God, the sovereignty of the will, a conditioned eternity

ch09:57: In Closing: The Place of One Who Has Received a Gift
ch09:58: The doctrine of personality can be summed up in a short chain. Personality is neither mind nor spirit; it cannot be built up through evolution; it is given only by the Universal Father, the primal personality. The personality so received shows itself in self-consciousness and relative free will; each one is irreplaceably unique; and all are within the Father's personality circuit. As a result, man can have fellowship with God, chooses his own destiny, and by that choice takes part in eternity. Yet the place where personality functions is mind. Choice, fellowship, and self-consciousness all take place through the medium of mind. The next chapter examines where this mind, which lies between matter and spirit, comes from and what structure it has.

ch09:59.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If personality is not “a progressive achievement” (5:6.3), then what actually grows when we say that a person grows and changes throughout life?
2. How does the fact that every personality is within the Father's personality circuit (5:6.11) give ground for the way I treat other people?
3. If God has made the sovereignty of the mortal will an absolute decree (5:6.8), how far does the responsibility entrusted to my choice extend?

ch10:label: Chapter 10
ch10:title: Mind
ch10:0: The previous chapter said that personality is a gift given from above. Yet personality does not function in a vacuum. Choosing, loving, and worshiping all take place in the setting of mind. In The Urantia Book, mind is a reality that lies between matter and spirit. Below, it touches the energies of the body; above, it touches the values of spirit. Paper 9 sums up the relation among these three realities in three words.
ch10:2: If energy is thing and spirit is value, mind is the meaning that links the two. This chapter asks four questions. What is mind? Where does mind come from? What levels and structure does mind have? And what part does mind play in human destiny?
ch10:4: The Foreword defines mind as “The thinking, perceiving, and feeling mechanism of the human organism” (0:5.8). But this mechanism does not spring up of itself from the matter of the brain. Paper 9, section 4, “The Absolute Mind,” draws a clear line between mind and energy.
ch10:6: This is the first principle of the doctrine of mind. Mind is not a product of matter but a ministry added on top of matter. The brain is a vessel that receives mind; mind itself comes from above. Paper 112 puts this principle forward as an argument against materialism.
ch10:8: There are two gulfs here. One is the gulf between matter and thought; the other is the still greater gulf between material mind and spiritual love. The first gulf is bridged by the mind ministry of the Infinite Spirit; the second is bridged by the ministry of spirit and by human choice. Mind stands precisely between these two gulfs. Paper 42 applies this principle to mind on every level.
ch10:10: Mind is ‘the presence-activity of living ministry.’ That is, some being is rendering living service upon an energy system. From the reflexes of the lowest animal to the highest worship, wherever there is mind, there is always someone's ministry. Who that someone is becomes the next question.
ch10:11: 2. Source: The Infinite Spirit and His Ministers
ch10:12: Just as the bestower of personality is the Universal Father, the bestower of mind is the Third Source and Center, the Infinite Spirit. Paper 9 stresses this point repeatedly.
ch10:14: The last sentence is important. The Thought Adjuster does not indwell just any mind. The mind ministry of the Infinite Spirit must first prepare the way. Mind, then, is the reality that prepares the ground on which personality and the Adjuster meet. The mind of the Infinite Spirit does not come to man all at once; it descends through ministers on several levels. The Seven Master Spirits, as the cosmic mind, distribute mind to the grand universe (9:4.3); in the local universe the Universe Mother Spirit takes up that mind; and the seven adjutant mind-spirits minister to the minds of men and animals (9:5.3, 36:5.1).

ch10:15.cap: Table 10.1  The Path by Which Mind Reaches Man
rows: The Third Source and Center (the Infinite Spirit): the bestower of mind
The Seven Master Spirits: the sevenfold source of the cosmic mind
The Universe Mother Spirit (Creative Spirit): the Nebadon modification of the cosmic mind
The seven adjutant mind-spirits: the personal ministry of the Mother Spirit
All mind is within the mind-gravity circuit of the Conjoint Actor

ch10:16: Along this path mind and personality arrive by different lines. Mind comes from the Infinite Spirit through his ministers; personality comes directly from the Father. Mind can therefore be given even to beings who have no personality.
ch10:18: Animals have mind and are conscious, but they have no personality. Man has received personality on top of mind. Here the principle seen in the previous chapter is confirmed once more: the endowment of mind alone does not make personality. Paper 9 therefore calls the human mind a strand of the cosmic mind: the mind of man is “an individualized circuit, an impersonal portion, of that cosmic mind” (9:5.4). Is the human mind, then, divine? Here the revelator at once draws a boundary line.
ch10:20: The source of mind is divine, but the human mind is not yet divine. The same section puts it plainly: “The Conjoint Creator is the source of mind, but mind is not the Conjoint Creator” (9:5.5). In the very next section Paper 9 calls this a compromise between the essence of thought perfection and the immature human nature (9:5.6).
ch10:22: Its origin and destiny are divine, but its present state is not. This distinction among three tenses sets the right attitude toward mind. Man has no reason either to worship his mind or to despise it. The revelator laments that men mar their minds by insincerity and unrighteousness and distort them by useless anxiety, and says that the contemplation of the immature human intellect “should lead only to reactions of humility” (9:5.7). But that humility is not resignation. Because the destiny of mind is divine, the direction in which it is turned remains man's own responsibility.
ch10:23: 3. Structure: The Levels of Mind and the Seven Adjutant Mind-Spirits
ch10:24: Paper 42, section 10, classifies the noncreator minds by level. This classification shows where the human mind stands on the universe ladder of mind.

rows: The seven adjutant mind-spirits of the Mother Spirit
Experiencing mind; five in animals, seven in man
The Mother Spirit and the Creator Son
Expanding consciousness in the ascending career
Embraces all finite levels of mind

ch10:26: The ministry of the adjutant mind-spirits begins long before man appears. Paper 36 says that they set the direction of evolution.
ch10:28: Evolution has a purpose because the ministry of mind has been present in life from the beginning. The human mind belongs to the second level, the adjutant-spirit mind. Animals also receive the ministry of the first five adjutant mind-spirits, but man receives all seven. The seven adjutant mind-spirits are listed in the order of their evolutionary attainment.

rows: Quick perception, the primitive physical and inherent reflex instincts, the self-preservative endowment (36:5.6)
The impulse of co-ordination, the association of ideas, quick reasoning (36:5.7)
The fidelity endowment, the basis of character acquirement (36:5.8)
The curiosity-mother of adventure and discovery, the scientific spirit (36:5.9)
The social urge, the endowment of species co-operation (36:5.10)
The religious impulse, the first differential urge (36:5.11)
The inherent tendency toward orderly and progressive advancement, co-ordinating the other adjutants (36:5.12)

ch10:30: Of these, the sixth is the threshold that separates man from the animals. The revelator speaks of the spirit of worship in these words.
ch10:32: It is not the degree of intelligence that separates man from the animal. What separates them is the impulse to lift one's head toward something higher than oneself, which is worship. And the moment this threshold is crossed, mind enters another domain of ministry.
ch10:34: The adjutant mind-spirits are not themselves personalities; they grow experientially but never become personal (36:5.13). They prepare the ground on which the ministry of spirit begins in man. That is also why the indwelling of the Thought Adjuster requires the functioning of all seven adjutant spirits (108:2.2).
ch10:35: 4. The Three Insights of the Cosmic Mind
ch10:36: The human mind does not consist solely of the ministry of the adjutant mind-spirits. Above it is the cosmic mind. Paper 16, section 6, “The Cosmic Mind,” says that the cosmic mind responds unerringly to three levels of reality (16:6.5). This response is not something man learns and acquires; it is a foundation laid in the mind from the beginning.

ch10:37.cap: Table 10.4  The Three Insights of the Cosmic Mind
rows: The reality domain of the physical senses, logical uniformity (16:6.6)
The reality domain of morals, the recognition of right and wrong (16:6.7)
The reality domain of religious experience, divine fellowship (16:6.8)

ch10:38: Because of these three insights, man is able to pursue science, philosophy, and religion. The reason he can trust facts, the reason he can weigh what is right, and the reason he can seek God all lie deep within the mind. The revelator explains what this foundation protects man from.
ch10:40: Man does not begin to think from nothing. The foundation for trusting causation, sensing duty, and desiring to worship is already present in the mind. Without it, science, philosophy, and religion would all be buildings standing on groundless assumptions. Yet this foundation does not grow of itself. The revelator regrets that so few mortals on Urantia take delight in cultivating these qualities (16:6.9). He therefore links this innate foundation to the goal of every human endeavor.
ch10:42: The last phrase connects with the previous chapter. Mind possesses the three insights, but what binds them into one is personality. Mind is the material; personality is the unifier.
ch10:43: 5. Mind as the Arena of Choice
ch10:44: What, then, does this mind do in human destiny? Paper 111, section 1, “The Mind Arena of Choice,” defines mind as the place where every decision is made.
ch10:46: Evolution provided the body, and the Father gave the Adjuster. But mind is different.
ch10:48: To say that life and death hang on mind does not mean that mind decides life and death, but that the decisions made within mind decide them. The same paper compares the roles of these three factors to a ship.
ch10:50: In this figure mind is the ship. The ship is neither the captain nor the pilot. A ship can go in either direction. Thus the evolving mind lies between the mechanical and the spiritual, and the minds in between are those “whose stability and tranquillity are dependent upon personality choice and spirit identification” (111:1.7). In his conversation with Ganid on Cyprus, Jesus described what happens when the mind is divided.
ch10:52: Unity of mind is not obtained by avoiding conflict. The same section adds that such peace is “attained by the stalwart assertion of the triumph of that which is true” (133:7.12). Depending on what it is dedicated to, the mind either scatters or becomes one.
ch10:54: Mind is a bestowal of divinity, but it is not eternal in itself. This is the weightiest consequence of the doctrine of mind.
ch10:56: Paper 111 says the same thing. Mortal mind is “a temporary intellect system loaned to human beings for use during a material lifetime” (111:1.5). What is borrowed must be returned. But the fruit of the decisions made with the borrowed mind remains. To the extent that mind identifies with spirit, that fruit is gathered into the newborn soul, and mind itself gains the way to pass over into morontia mind. The birth of this soul is treated in Chapter 12. As Paper 9 says, in the time universes mind “seems to function in a mid-zone between energy and spirit” (9:6.7). The destiny of mind is not to remain in that mid-zone but to cross over, through choice, to the side of spirit.

ch10:57.cap: Table 10.5  The Chain of Logic in the Doctrine of Mind
rows: A living ministry superimposed upon energy, the reality of meaning
The Infinite Spirit is the bestower of mind and ministers through the Master Spirits and the Mother Spirit
The seven adjutant mind-spirits and the three insights of the cosmic mind
The arena of choice in which personality chooses God or forsakes him
Not immortal apart from spirit identification; a temporary system on loan

ch10:58: In Closing: The Place of Meaning
ch10:59: To thread the doctrine of mind together once more: energy is thing, spirit is value, and mind creates meaning between the two. Mind does not spring from matter but is superimposed upon energy, and its source is the Infinite Spirit. The human mind receives the ministry of the seven adjutant mind-spirits and the three insights of the cosmic mind, and so becomes able to pursue science, philosophy, and religion. Yet that mind is not yet divine, and unless it identifies with spirit, it is not eternal either. Mind is the arena in which personality chooses God or forsakes him. Into that very arena the Father himself has come down to dwell. The next chapter examines God indwelling the mind, the Thought Adjuster.

ch10:60.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. How does the distinction “Energy is thing, mind is meaning, spirit is value” (9:4.5) shed light on the way I spend my day?
2. If the spirit of worship distinguishes man from the animal (36:5.11), what does it mean to say that worship, not intelligence, is the threshold of being human?
3. If mind is the ship and the will is the captain (111:1.9), what conflicts are now unsettling the ship of my mind?

ch11:label: Chapter 11
ch11:title: The Thought Adjuster
ch11:0: In the previous two chapters man received two gifts. Personality comes directly from the Universal Father, and mind comes from the Infinite Spirit through a series of ministers. Yet the most astonishing reality in man, as The Urantia Book describes him, is a third gift: God causes a part of himself to dwell directly in the human mind. Paper 107 opens with this fact.
ch11:2: This paradox, that the One who is farthest away is also nearest, is the starting point of the doctrine of the Adjuster. This chapter asks five questions. What is the Adjuster? Why does God come into man? When, and under what conditions, does he come? What does he do in the mind? And where does the relationship between man and the Adjuster end?
ch11:4: Concerning the origin of the Adjusters there is no difference of opinion in the universe: they proceed directly from the Universal Father. The revelator presses the meaning still further.
ch11:6: The Adjuster is not a creature made by God but a fragment of God himself. That is why the Adjuster is of a different order from the angels or other spirit ministers. At the same time, the Adjuster is not a personality. Paper 107 says, “Thought Adjusters are not personalities, but they are real entities” (107:7.1), and calls them prepersonal realities. Personality belongs to the man; the Adjuster belongs to the God who dwells within that man. This difference arises, as we saw in Chapter 9, from the fact that personality and the Adjuster are different gifts. The Adjuster is not a cold principle but a presence of love. The introduction to Paper 107 portrays the Adjusters in these words.
ch11:8: The word ‘imprisoned’ shows the humility of this indwelling. A fragment of the infinite God consents to abide in the narrow place of a finite mortal mind. And that abiding is itself a promise of man's eternal career. The various names by which the Adjuster is called illuminate various aspects of his nature.

ch11:9.cap: Table 11.1  The Names of the Adjuster
rows: Not a helper of thought but an adjuster of thought
The way in which the Father indwells the human mind
Evidence that the Father has reserved a way of direct communication with every material creature
The spirit luminosity that accompanies the divine presence
The mission concerns the future life more than this life

ch11:10: 2. The Ground: Why God Comes into Man
ch11:11: The reason God indwells man lies in the goal God has set for man. That goal is one man could never reach by his own power.
ch11:13: The logic is simple. First comes the command to be perfect, and then the Adjuster comes as the way to fulfill that command. God does not merely set the goal and withdraw; he himself becomes a partner on the road to that goal. The same section therefore calls the Adjuster's indwelling “the absolute and unqualified assurance” (107:0.3) that man can find the Father. The very fact of an indwelling God is the guarantee that God can be found.
ch11:15: The fatherhood of God does not end as a confession or a metaphor. Because a fragment of the Father actually dwells in man, man is actually a son of God. The doctrine of the fatherhood of God becomes fact in the indwelling of the Adjuster.
ch11:16: 3. The Indwelling: When and Where He Comes
ch11:17: The Adjuster does not come at just any time. Paper 108, section 2, “Prerequisites of Adjuster Indwelling,” says that the mind must first be prepared.
ch11:19: Here the ministry of the seven adjutant mind-spirits, seen in Chapter 10, bears fruit. When the spirit of worship and the spirit of wisdom are functioning and the child makes his first moral choice, the Adjuster comes. On Urantia this occurs, on the average, just before the sixth birthday (108:2.1). And since the bestowal of Michael and the pouring out of the Spirit of Truth, Adjusters indwell the minds of all normal will creatures (108:6.2).
ch11:20: This indwelling does not wait until man has been made clean. The same section says that through the divine gifts the Father makes his closest approach to sin and evil, and adds, “for it is literally true that the Adjuster must coexist in the mortal mind even in the very midst of human unrighteousness” (108:6.2). The Adjuster suffers from man's selfish thoughts and animal fears and yet does not depart. The text assures us: “The Adjuster remains with you in all disaster and through every sickness which does not wholly destroy the mentality” (110:1.5). So persistent is the way God stays at man's side.

ch11:21.cap: Table 11.2  The Conditions and Time of the Adjuster's Indwelling
rows: The co-ordinate function of the seven adjutants, encircuitment in the Holy Spirit
The 2,134th day of terrestrial life, just prior to the sixth birthday
All normal will creatures after the bestowal Son and the bestowal of the Spirit of Truth
Not the material brain but the mortal mind

ch11:22: The place where the Adjuster abides must also be made clear. The Adjuster is not located in any organ of the body.
ch11:24: That the Adjuster indwells the mind dovetails with the conclusion of Chapter 10, that mind is the arena where the Adjuster and man meet. The Adjuster works upon the mind, and man chooses within the mind.
ch11:25: 4. The Mission: What He Does in the Mind
ch11:26: The key to understanding the Adjuster's mission lies in the word ‘adjust.’ The Adjuster does not do man's thinking for him.
ch11:28: Thinking is the part of personality. The Adjuster improves, modifies, and co-ordinates that thinking, and above all builds up its spiritual counterpart. The same section says that the Adjusters “are devoted to the work of building up spiritual counterparts of your careers, morontia transcripts of your true advancing selves” (110:2.3). Whatever of spiritual value is found in the decisions man makes on earth is reproduced in the Adjuster and preserved for the next life. Even truths man cannot yet receive are not discarded.
ch11:30: The Adjuster does not lose what could not be accomplished in this life but carries it over into the next. For the Adjuster, life on earth is not an end but a stage. The Adjuster's mission, therefore, is not to make this life comfortable.
ch11:32: Within man the Adjuster becomes a stimulus of a different kind from outward stimuli. The senses of the body reach the mind along the nerves, but the Adjuster's stimulus comes from within and from above.
ch11:34: That life is not easy may be no proof that the Adjuster is absent; it may be a sign that the Adjuster is at work. For without decisions there is no growth, and without growth the soul does not grow. Yet even the Adjuster cannot make man's decisions for him. The Adjusters would like to change fear into love and confidence, “but they cannot mechanically and arbitrarily do such things; that is your task” (108:5.8).

ch11:35.cap: Table 11.3  What the Adjuster Does and Does Not Do
rows: What the Adjuster does not do
Builds morontia transcripts of the life
Takes over the personality's prerogative of thought
Makes life reasonably difficult to stimulate decisions
Would change fear into love and confidence

ch11:36: 5. Co-operation: The Human Will and the Adjuster
ch11:37: If the Adjuster is a fragment of God, why does the Adjuster's will bow to the will of man? The answer of The Urantia Book lies in the sovereignty of the will that the Father has decreed (5:6.8). The Adjuster does not overstep that sovereignty.
ch11:39: But if the Adjuster also has volition, why is he subservient to the will of man? Paper 107 explains this by the difference in the levels on which will operates.
ch11:41: Personality is the gift of the Father, and the Adjuster is a prepersonal reality. Therefore even a fragment of God respects the choice of personality. When the human mind fully conforms to the mind of the Adjuster and the will carries out the decisions of that combined mind, only then does the Adjuster's prepersonal will attain personality expression through man's decision (110:2.5). The will of God appears in human life only through the will of man. The relationship with the Adjuster is therefore one of co-operation. That co-operation is not necessarily a conscious process. The revelator says that man's motives and decisions, his faithful determinations and supreme desires, do constitute real co-operation (110:3.6). And he sets forth four ways of consciously augmenting that co-operation.

ch11:42.cap: Table 11.4  Four Ways of Augmenting Adjuster Harmony
rows: Choosing to respond to divine leading
Basing the life on the highest consciousness of truth, beauty, and goodness (110:3.7)
Loving God and desiring to be like him
Recognizing the divine fatherhood and lovingly worshiping the heavenly Parent (110:3.8)
Loving man and desiring to serve him
Recognizing the brotherhood of man and cherishing a wise affection (110:3.9)
Recognizing obligations to the Supreme Being; the birth of cosmic morality (110:3.10)

ch11:43: In this co-operation it is not the Adjuster who fails: “Adjusters never fail” (110:3.3). Angels and even the Sons of the local universe may sometimes depart from the divine way, “but Adjusters never falter” (108:5.3). Success or failure is spoken of only from the standpoint of human survival. What, then, is the heart of this co-operation?
ch11:45: The progress of co-operation shows itself in the conquest of the seven psychic circles. Entrance upon the seventh circle marks the beginning of true human personality function, and completion of the first circle denotes the relative maturity of the mortal being (110:6.1). As man passes through the circles one by one, attunement with the Adjuster deepens, the soul grows, and the personality becomes more real (110:6.8–110:6.10). As the circles are traversed, the voice of the Adjuster also draws nearer. That voice is always within man, yet most people “will hear it seldom during a lifetime” (110:7.9). Not to hear him does not mean that he is not there. Most of the Adjuster's work is done quietly, below the threshold of consciousness.
ch11:47: The end of co-operation is fusion. But the attainment of the circles is not the same as fusion. Fusion depends “upon the attainment of a final and complete attunement of the mortal will with the will of God as it is resident in the Thought Adjuster” (110:7.1). When that attunement is achieved, the two are no longer two.
ch11:49: Note here that the partner in fusion is ‘the immortal morontia soul.’ The Adjuster does not fuse with man's material mind; he fuses with the soul he has nurtured together with man. The doctrine of the Adjuster thus leads into the doctrine of the soul. And fusion is not an end but the beginning of unending discovery.

ch11:51.cap: Table 11.5  The Chain of Logic in the Doctrine of the Adjuster
rows: An uncreated fragment of God, a real entity that is not a personality
God descended as a partner to fulfill the command to be perfect
Indwells the mind after the adjutants' preparation and the first moral decision
Spiritualizes and eternalizes thinking and builds morontia transcripts
Never spiritualizes against the will; the desire to be Godlike
Fusion with the soul, a never-ending revelation of God

ch11:52: In Closing: God Who Is Nearest
ch11:53: The doctrine of the Adjuster unites the transcendence and the immanence of God in a single reality. The Father at the center of Paradise sends a fragment of himself into the human mind. That fragment is not created; it is God himself, and it comes as a partner for fulfilling the command to be perfect. The Adjuster indwells the mind prepared by the adjutant mind-spirits at the time of the first moral decision; he spiritualizes thought rather than replacing it, and he stimulates decisions rather than making life easy. Because he never acts against the will of man, everything is accomplished through co-operation, and when that co-operation is complete, man and the Adjuster become one. Yet the partner in that fusion is the soul that man and the Adjuster bring forth together. The next chapter examines how this soul is born, how it grows, and where it goes.

ch11:54.title: Questions for Reflection
items: 1. If the Adjuster is the reality that “factualizes the truth that God is man's Father” (107:0.6), what weight does my prayer carry when I call God Father?
2. If the Adjuster makes life reasonably difficult in order to stimulate decisions (108:5.5), which of the difficulties in my life right now are calling for a decision?
3. Of the four ways of augmenting harmony with the Adjuster (110:3.7–110:3.10), which am I neglecting most at present?
